title: Lead workgroup activities relating to material preparation processes

lessons.title: Planning and organising the work
lessons.html:
Planning and organising the work

Material preparation in grain handling means getting grain ready for storage, dispatch or processing: pre-cleaning, screening, drying, cooling, blending to grade, and treating against insects. As a team leader you are responsible for getting the shift's preparation work done safely, on time, at the right quality and with little waste.

Understand the requirement

  • What must be prepared: commodity, grade, tonnage and destination bin or truck.
  • Quality targets: for example moisture content, screenings and foreign matter limits set by the grading regulations or the client contract.
  • Deadlines: when trucks or rail trucks arrive, when the mill needs the grain.

Plan the shift

  1. Check that equipment is available and serviced: dryers, cleaners, conveyors, elevators, aspirators, moisture meters.
  2. Check materials: fuel for the dryer, approved grain protectants, bags if needed.
  3. Work out the sequence. For example, clean before drying so the dryer does not waste heat on chaff and dust.
  4. Allocate people to tasks according to their skills and authorisations. Only authorised staff run the dryer or apply protectants.
  5. Plan breaks so key positions are always covered.

Brief the team

Hold a short start-of-shift meeting, about ten minutes. Cover:

  • The targets for the shift.
  • Who does what.
  • The main hazards today: dust, moving machinery, confined spaces, working at heights, hot surfaces.
  • Any changes: a new grade, a machine out of service, a visitor on site.

Ask questions to check that people understood. A brief that only goes one way is easy to forget.

Example

The silo must load 300 t of yellow maize to a client spec on Friday. On Wednesday the team leader sees the bin moisture is above the limit. He plans drying on Wednesday and Thursday, books the dryer operator for both shifts, and arranges sampling every two hours so progress is known well before Friday.

lessons.title: Monitoring work, quality and the team
lessons.html:
Monitoring work, quality and the team

Monitor progress

  • Walk the plant at set times. See the work for yourself.
  • Compare output with the plan: tonnes cleaned, tonnes dried, bins filled.
  • Read the records: dryer temperatures, moisture readings, sample results.
  • If you are falling behind, find the cause early and adjust: move a worker, ask maintenance for help, or tell your manager the deadline is at risk.

Control quality

  • Make sure samples are taken and tested as planned.
  • Act on results. If moisture is still too high, the grain goes back through the dryer; if screenings are high, adjust the cleaner.
  • Never let grain that does not meet spec go to a bin or truck marked as in spec.
  • Keep different grades and commodities separate. Clean equipment between them.

Safety leadership

  • Enforce lock-out before anyone works on conveyors, elevators or cleaners.
  • Nobody enters a bin or silo without the confined space permit, a standby person and the correct equipment.
  • Keep dust levels down and enforce the no-smoking and hot-work permit rules. Grain dust can explode.
  • Stop unsafe work. As a team leader you have both the right and the duty to do so under your site rules and the OHS Act 85 of 1993.

Leading people

  • Give clear instructions and say why.
  • Recognise good work in front of the team.
  • Deal with poor performance privately and fairly, using facts.
  • Help resolve conflict early: listen to both sides and focus on the work.
  • Coach less experienced workers and let them practise under supervision.

Handover and reporting

At the end of the shift, record what was done, quality results, problems and anything unfinished. Hand over to the next team leader face to face where possible. Report incidents, near misses and equipment faults on the right forms.

Key points

  • Plan the shift around requirements, equipment, materials and people.
  • Brief the team on targets, tasks and hazards and check understanding.
  • Monitor output and quality and act early when there is a problem.
  • Enforce lock-out, confined space and dust rules.
  • Lead fairly, give feedback and hand over properly.
